title: Native clients keep a refreshed session and can revoke it on sign-out (web half of iOS RF-1012)
acceptance: AUD-007: a session older than Better Auth updateAge gets a Set-Cookie with a later expiry from POST /api/v1/auth/session and from any requireSession route, exactly once per response and alongside any cookie the route sets itself (provider connect's OAuth state cookie); a younger session gets no session Set-Cookie; a 401 carries no Set-Cookie, so a stale request cannot clear a newer sign-in's cookie (integration and unit tests).

AUD-009: a native-shaped POST /api/auth/sign-out (cookie, JSON, no Origin/Referer/Sec-Fetch-*) revokes the session, and re-injecting the old cookie gets 401 from POST /api/v1/auth/session (integration test).

Browser CSRF protection is unchanged: sign-out with an untrusted or null Origin, an untrusted Referer, fetch metadata, or a form-shaped body revokes nothing, and other cookie-bearing auth POSTs without Origin are still refused (integration and unit tests).

OpenAPI documents the shared SessionSetCookie response header on every session-authenticated operation, and api.md, authorization.md and conventions.md describe the refresh cookie, the no-cookie 401 and the sign-out trust boundary; the iOS web-contract snapshots are refreshed in a separate iOS PR.

evidence.summary: iOS code audit AUD-007 (probable 7-day hard expiry) and AUD-009 (probable unrevoked sign-out); both carried by iOS RF-1012.
Owner approved this web change for RF-1012 in the Air session on 2026-11-02.

Before the fix on 8f26519 both findings reproduced: the aged session row was extended but no Set-Cookie reached the client (AUD-007), and native sign-out got 403 MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN with the session still valid (AUD-009). All 13 cases pass after the fix.

Forwards refreshed session cookies from /auth/session and requireSession routes, adds withNativeSignOutOrigin for native sign-out, and documents both in OpenAPI and the dev-plan docs. Full local gate green on 0f1438e.

Against a local wrangler dev (port 8799, throwaway vars, MOCK_PROVIDERS): a session aged 2 days got Set-Cookie Max-Age=604800 from POST /api/v1/auth/session; a no-Origin JSON sign-out returned 200 and the old cookie then got 401 from POST /api/v1/auth/session.

Final review of #703 at 55adab7 found that forwardSetCookies' c.res assignment let Hono 4.13.14's res setter drop the session cookie on routes that set their own cookie. The new provider-connect case fails with that code (no session cookie) and passes with c.header append. Also added: refresh forwarded exactly once behind many requireSession routers, and the clearing cookie on 401 from /auth/session and /auth/me. 17 integration cases pass.
Three stacked requireSession routers resolve the session once (getSession called once), forward the refresh once, keep the route's own cookie, and forward the clearing cookie on 401.

Second final review of #703 at 31ff13a: forwarding Better Auth's Max-Age=0 clearing cookie on 401 could let a slow request carrying user A's dead cookie delete user B's cookie after a sign-out and new sign-in (same cookie name). 401s now carry no Set-Cookie (integration and unit tests assert it); the unreachable fallback in forwardSetCookies is removed. Residual narrow race: a refresh issued for A just before sign-out that arrives after B's sign-in; Better Auth's own endpoints share it.

Deferred from the 31ff13a review, not fixed here (owner or conductor to decide, possibly as new Backlog tasks): (1) the native sign-out origin-handling design itself, for the owner; (2) the userId short-circuit in requireSession relies on nothing else setting userId first; (3) c.header copies a finalized Response once per forwarded cookie; (4) the OpenAPI SessionSetCookie opt-out keys on security: [] and so depends on public operations declaring it.

resolution: Both audit findings were real and reproduced in integration tests before the fix. The web side now returns refreshed session cookies from every successful session-authenticated response (never a clearing cookie on 401), resolves the session once per request, and revokes a native sign-out, with browser CSRF behaviour pinned by tests. Two fix rounds after final review kept route-set cookies intact and removed the 401 clearing cookie. Review items deferred from the 31ff13a review are listed in the evidence and the PR. The iOS half (persist Set-Cookie from any authed response, treat 401 as signed out, log failed sign-out, reinstall handling) ships in iOS RF-1012/RF-1032 after its web-contract snapshots are refreshed.
